'''''Contemptor''''' is an extinct genus of [[Scombriformes|scombrid]] fish that belongs to the family [[Gempylidae]] (snake mackerels). It is known from the [[Eocene]] ([[Ypresian]] age) of northern Italy. The genus contains one species, '''''Contemptor mastinoi'''''.<ref name=":0">{{Cite journal |last1=Calzoni |first1=Pietro |last2=Giusberti |first2=Luca |last3=Fornaciari |first3=Eliana |last4=Luciani |first4=Valeria |last5=Boscolo-Galazzo |first5=Flavia |last6=Bernardi |first6=Massimo |last7=Tomasoni |first7=Riccardo |last8=Carnevale |first8=Giorgio |date=2026-03-04 |editor-last=Banerjee |editor-first=Santanu |title=The Ypresian ichthyofauna of the Monte Solane Lagerstätte (Verona, northern Italy): A deep dive into the western Tethys early Eocene mesopelagic setting |journal=PLOS ONE |language=en |volume=21 |issue=3 |article-number=e0338490 |doi=10.1371/journal.pone.0338490 |doi-access=free |pmid=41779693 |pmc=12959715 |issn=1932-6203}}</ref>

Like all gempylids, it has an elongated and slightly compressed [[fusiform]] body shape. It has small conical teeth. It had a length of around 81.5–84.4 mm.<ref name=":0" />

== Discovery and naming ==
[[File:Contemptor mastinoi.jpg|thumb|[[Life restoration]]]]
The holotype (IGVR 82435–82436) of this genus was discovered in the [[Marly limestones]] of the [[Chiusole Formation]] in the [[Monte Solaro|Monte Solane]] mountains, near Verona, Italy. A paratype (IGVR 67858), which is nearly complete, was also found. The holotype consists of a nearly complete articulated skeleton.<ref name=":0" />

The generic name "''Contemptor''" is a [[Latin]] word meaning "''contemptuous''", in reference to the fierce appearance of this genus, according to the describers. The specific name honors [[Mastino I della Scala|Mastino della Scala]], a Master of the city of [[Verona]], Italy from 1262 to 1277. It is also in reference to the [[Italian language|Italian]] word "''mastino''" which means "''mastiff''", due to the large fangs of this species.<ref name=":0" />
